title: Early Fox Islands: Beveridge names, land petitions, and the Carver connection
overview: Research-linked documents, not new confirmed family relationships or surveyed holdings.

sources.title: 1785 Fox Islands survey (Maine State Archives)
sources.detail: Stone and Mathews survey made in October–November 1785, attested by Rufus Putnam; Maine State Archives, Knox County planbook p. 7, identifier 302962.

sources.title: 1785 list of Fox Islands
sources.detail: Original planbook listing North/South Fox Islands and surrounding named islands; Maine State Archives, Plan Book 9 p. 1.5.

sources.title: 1786 Fox Islands plan including Pulpit Harbor
sources.detail: Maine State Archives, Plan Book 8 p. 16, Jonathan Stone; indexed places include Pulpit Harbor and Crabtree's Point; linked in catalog to conditional grant March 13, 1786.

sources.title: 1838 copy of Fox Islands plan
sources.detail: Maine State Archives, Plan Book 9 p. 1, copy prepared by George W. Coffin.

sources.title: Brief Historical Sketch of the Town of Vinalhaven
sources.detail: Printed pp. 9–11: transcript of islanders' 1785 petition and Massachusetts 1786 resolution. Do not count a later reprint as an independent petition.

sources.title: The Carver Family of New England — Clifford N. Carver
sources.detail: Printed pp. 94–98 cover early settlers, petition list and 1786 grant; p. 108 discusses 700 acres at Carver's Harbor. Scan: PDF pp. 112–118 and 130.

sources.title: History of Thomaston, Rockland, and South Thomaston, vol. II — Cyrus Eaton
sources.detail: Printed pp. 146–147: Capt. Matthew Beverage of Hope, two spouses, ten named children, nephew Nathaniel and descendants.

sources.title: Genius at Riverhead: A Profile of Harold H. Beverage
sources.detail: Family-biographical genealogy identifies Matthew in the James Beveridge and Jean White line, to be verified with contemporary parentage records.

sources.title: The Maine Genealogist, vol. 47, no. 4 (Nov 2025), pp. 170–182
sources.kind: documented genealogical article with primary citations
sources.detail: David Flanagan and Barbara Beverage Reeves, 'The Ebenezer Eames Family: Early Settlers of North Fox Island, Maine', printed p. 170 / PDF p.27, footnotes 5–6. It dates the Fox Islands petition June 1, 1785, and cites a 1786 Putnam report with early settlers' years of residence, Box 001 (paper), Maine State Archives. The original report has not yet been inspected.

sources.title: History of Brunswick, Topsham, and Harpswell (Wheeler, 1878)
sources.detail: Public domain complete 1878 town history, including early Topsham/Brunswick map key and Henry family section.

sources.title: Early Topsham Settlers, transcription of Wheeler's 1878 list
sources.detail: Lists Samuel Beveridge in 1752 on lot 3 and James Beveridge in 1758 on lot 7. Dates, identity and title require original records.

sources.title: 1878 map key naming Samuel Beveridge and a Brunswick Beverage location
sources.detail: Numbered historical map list calls Topsham location 3 Samuel Beveridge and Brunswick 25 Beverage; the underlying plan/era and original image should be inspected before geolocation.

sources.title: Wheeler 1878 Henry family sketch, printed page 836
sources.detail: States James, son of earlier Topsham resident James Henry, was probably married Feb. 15, 1776 to Mercy Beveridge. Needs vital/marriage/probate confirmation.

sources.title: Hope, Maine historical county sequence
sources.detail: Hope was in Lincoln County until 1827, Waldo until 1860, and Knox thereafter; do not search only later Knox estate-file collection for a ca.1837 death.

sources.title: Waldo County Registry of Deeds official access
sources.detail: Official registry links the state-wide land records portal and describes historic deeds/plans, but a given 18th-century Beveridge record is not yet identified.

findings.title: Three Beveridge names among the Fox Islands land claimants
findings.summary: The copied 1785 petition names James Beveridge, Thomas Beveridge and Matthew Beveridge (a minor). George White and John Calderwood sign as attorneys for the inhabitants; the list itself must not be described as three surviving autograph signatures. The grant addresses qualifying settlers and their heirs, not a specified allotment to any one Beveridge household.
findings.status: Next: find original claimants' allotments and compare the 1785–86 plans with county deeds.

findings.title: Matthew Beveridge — potentially an overlooked family branch
findings.summary: The 1785 petition lists Matthew as a minor. A separate 1865 history describes Capt. Matthew Beverage of Hope, with marriages to Abigail Dyer and Clarissa Cobb, and ten named children: Harrison, Achsa, Louisa, Mary Miles, James Madison, Ezekiel G. D., Sarah Abby, Thomas Jefferson, George W. and Martha W. A later family appendix and user-contributed pedigrees suggest Matthew was a son of James Beveridge and Jean White, and a brother of Capt. Thomas Beverage. The source identities have not yet been independently proved to belong to one person; the date of birth about 1766 and death about 1837 remain leads, not verified dates.
findings.status: Next: locate original baptism, probate, marriage, land or guardianship evidence. Do not merge his family into the main tree yet.

findings.title: Do not misread the petition as a list of personal signatures
findings.summary: A 2025 scholarly genealogical article dates the Fox Islands petition to 1 June 1785, while the 1935 Carver history describes a March 1785 local meeting before the petition. The transcribed list is not individual autograph signatures; George White and John Calderwood signed as attorneys. The website's James Beveridge Jr. currently has a death date of 1 March 1785. These dates, and which James was named, remain unresolved and are NOT evidence to automatically change his death record.
findings.status: Request original June 1785 petition and verify James's probate/death chronology. March meeting and June presentation should not be conflated.

findings.title: Carver's Harbor property and shared island history
findings.summary: Carver (1935), p. 108, reports Thaddeus Carver purchased 700 acres, a sawmill and buildings from Francis Cogswell for £260 at what later became Carver's Harbor, South Fox Island/Vinalhaven. The same book lists Carver and Beveridge claimants together in the land petition; this is geographic/community evidence, not proof that the Beveridges held the Carver acreage.
findings.status: Next: locate the original Cogswell–Carver deed; never count these 700 acres as Beverage property.

findings.title: Carver/Beverage marriage needs its own lineage verification
findings.confidence: Existing tree entry, not proved in attached book
findings.summary: The site's family tree identifies Olive Leadbetter Carver as the wife of Albert Glover Beverage. The uploaded 1935 book includes a number of Israel Carver branches but does not independently establish her parentage or her marriage. Keep the existing relationship unchanged and investigate original 19th-century marriage and birth records before extending the Carver line.
findings.status: Next: check North Haven/Vinalhaven vital records and probate for Olive's father and grandfather.

findings.title: Early settlers declared how long they had lived on Fox Islands
findings.confidence: Published archival citation; original report not yet inspected
findings.summary: A 2025 article by David Flanagan and Barbara Beverage Reeves cites 'General Putnam's Report and Description', dated 18 March 1786, Box 001 (paper), Maine State Archives; it reports that island settlers declared the number of years since their arrival. The original data may help test James, Thomas and Matthew Beveridge's presence, but no specific Beveridge arrival year has been retrieved.
findings.status: Request the March 18, 1786 report (not just the October–November 1785 map); transcribe entries for James, Thomas, Matthew and household neighbors.

findings.title: James and Samuel Beveridge in the Topsham land record trail
findings.confidence: Historical map key and compiled index; identities not proven
findings.summary: The 1878 Wheeler history includes a map key naming 'Samuel Beveridge' at Topsham location 3 and an unnamed 'Beverage' at Brunswick location 25. A derivative early-settlers index gives Samuel Beveridge, 1752, lot 3 and James Beveridge, 1758, lot 7. This does not establish whether either was James Beveridge Sr., Jr. or Samuel Beveridge (b. ca. 1702 in the current family tree), nor does it provide acreage.
findings.status: Locate 1750s grant books/deeds and check the original 1878 map. Keep Samuel's relationship to James as an open question.

findings.title: Potential given name of Mercy Beveridge's husband: James Henry
findings.summary: Wheeler's 1878 Topsham family history says the younger James Henry 'probably' married Mercy Beveridge on 15 February 1776. The existing website names a spouse in Mercy Beveridge Henry's record, but the scanned history does not independently prove this is the same Mercy or name her father. Do not change the person record until an original marriage or probate link is found.
findings.status: Seek marriage intentions/returns and Topsham records for Feb 1776, then check Henry probate and 1790/1800 households.

findings.title: Locate Matthew's potential estate in the correct historic county
findings.confidence: County jurisdiction confirmed; estate not located
findings.summary: Hope moved from Lincoln County to Waldo County in 1827 and then into Knox County in 1860. If Capt. Matthew Beverage died in Hope around 1837 as later pedigree sources report, his probate should initially be sought in Waldo-era records, not the Knox estate-file collection beginning in 1861. Neither the death date nor an actual probate entry is yet proved.
findings.status: Search Waldo probate books/index under Beverage/Beveridge/Bevridge, and Hope town returns; request the estate file if identified.

caveat: The three 1785 petition names are not proven individual signature images; the 1786 resolution covers the island group (16,527 acres in the later transcriptions), not a family property award. Original map images may show historic locations but never automatically establish deeds, acreage or biological relationships.
